response: Research suggests that pediatric concussion patients often have poor compliance with discharge instructions. Studies have shown that between 20-50% of pediatric concussion patients do not fully adhere to recommended discharge instructions, such as rest, avoiding contact sports, and follow-up appointments. This non-compliance can be attributed to various factors, including lack of understanding, misinterpretation of instructions, and parental or patient misconceptions about concussion management. As a result, healthcare providers should prioritize clear communication, provide written instructions, and schedule follow-up appointments to ensure that pediatric concussion patients and their families understand and comply with discharge instructions.
